classification.difficultyReason: Combines sampling without replacement within each day with independent repeated daily trials and an exactly-three-days count.

content.prompt: A tank contains 20 tagged fish and 80 untagged fish. On each day, four fish are selected at random, and after noting whether they are tagged or untagged, they are returned to the tank. Answer the following questions, correct to three significant figures.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the probability of selecting no tagged fish on a given day?

answer.worked:
Choose all four fish from the 80 untagged fish, out of all four-fish selections from 100 fish.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{no tagged fish})&=\frac{{}^{80}C_4}{{}^{100}C_4}\\&\approx0.403\quad\text{(3 s.f.)}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the probability of selecting at least one tagged fish on a given day?

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}P(\text{at least one tagged fish})&=1-P(\text{no tagged fish})\\&=1-\frac{{}^{80}C_4}{{}^{100}C_4}\\&\approx0.597\quad\text{(3 s.f.)}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Calculate the probability of selecting no tagged fish on every day for a week.

answer.worked:
The fish are returned after each day's selection, so the daily selections are independent. Let $p=\frac{{}^{80}C_4}{{}^{100}C_4}$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{no tagged fish on all seven days})&=p^7\\&\approx0.00174\quad\text{(3 s.f.)}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is the probability of selecting no tagged fish on exactly three of the seven days during the week?

answer.worked:
Let $p=\frac{{}^{80}C_4}{{}^{100}C_4}$. Choose the three days with no tagged fish in ${}^{7}C_3$ ways. On each of the other four days, at least one fish must be tagged. The daily selections are independent.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{exactly three days})&={}^{7}C_3p^3(1-p)^4\\&\approx0.291\quad\text{(3 s.f.)}.\end{aligned}$$
